description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-hash` (~line 16477): `(loop for item in (%p-tie-views pairs) ... append ... collect ...)` copies every pair into `flat`, then `(make-hash-table :test 'equal)` -- SBCL's default size is 7, so any literal with 8+ keys (objects: `bless { ... }` with many fields, JSON-like records, Pod::Simple nodes) grows the table once or twice (sb-impl::grow-hash-table was 5 % of the podtext profile).

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/lev/hash-presize.lisp redefines p-hash: when no pair item is a vector or a hash table, size the table to (ceiling n 2) and insert straight from the argument list; otherwise the old body; ab.pl --lever, best of 5, legs/leg2.log, load 1.3):
  anonhash (300 k x a 10-key `{ id => $i, name => "n$i", a => 1, ... }`)  0.267 -> 0.226 s  -15.4 %  (C/A +0.4 %)
  moo-objs                                                              +1.8 %  (C/A +0.8 %: not measurable)
  podtext                                                                -0.0 %  (its growth is in element stores, not in p-hash)

THE FIX: in p-hash, the no-flatten fast path with :size; the same presize in the flatten path (the count is known after flattening).  Optional sibling: p-array-init's growth from 0.  Runtime only.

BAR: hash rows of the gate (grep -l 'p-hash' Pl/t), sweep (hash.t, hashassign.t +0), tied-hash guard rows (%p-tie-views must still see a tied operand), the anonhash row reproduced, everyday.

DO NOT: presize from the ARGUMENT count when an item is a hash or a vector (it flattens to more pairs); do not skip %p-tie-views.
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): the anonymous-hash constructor p-hash conses a full copy of its pair list and grows an unsized EQUAL table -- presizing + skipping the copy when nothing needs flattening is -15 % on a 10-key `{...}` constructor loop
